key_insight: Granular discharge remains free-fall-like across circular, triangular, and rectangular apertures, with confinement effects collapsing when the aperture is characterized by hydraulic diameter and local packing deficit.
engineering_relevance: Aperture perimeter and area can be used to predict steady mass flux and outlet velocity in hopper-like discharge systems, helping design openings with more reliable throughput across shapes.
method: Combined laboratory experiments with discrete-element simulations of spherical particles.
Tested steady discharge through triangular, rectangular, and lens-shaped apertures.
Integrated local packing deficit over the opening to identify an effective confinement length, D_h = 4A/P.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent flux trends across multiple aperture geometries, with the local packing model matching lens-shaped aperture fields without additional fitting.
watch_item: The scaling is validated for steady discharge of spherical particles, so strong shape irregularity, non-spherical grains, or transient clogging may require additional correction.
paper_title: Steady granular discharge across aperture shapes
